external_entities.name: readers
external_entities.description: People who access the public site and fetch published assets.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in.

external_entities.name: admin
external_entities.description: An administrator who maintains the database directly.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: The content delivery network from which readers fetch images, stylesheets, and downloads.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server
processes.description: The web server runs the CMS and serves the public site.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

data_stores.name: MySQL database
data_stores.description: A database containing pages, accounts, and comments.
data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.
data_stores.notes: The source does not state whether the database is encrypted on disk: "I could not tell you whether the database is encrypted on disk."

data_stores.name: CDN's bucket
data_stores.description: The bucket to which the web server pushes newly published assets for delivery by the CDN.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.

data_flows.name: access site
data_flows.description: Readers access the public site through the web server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in.

data_flows.name: fetch assets
data_flows.description: Readers fetch images, stylesheets, and downloads from the CDN.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

data_flows.name: publish assets
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When new assets are published the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source states: "Nothing here tells you how the push to the CDN is authenticated".

data_flows.name: maintain database
data_flows.description: The admin directly maintains the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.

trust_boundaries.name: public network
trust_boundaries.description: The network locations from which readers and the administrator connect to the system.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: they do it from wherever they happen to be — there is no jump host.

trust_boundaries.name: hosted network
trust_boundaries.description: The hosted network containing the web server and MySQL database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.

trust_boundaries.name: CDN
trust_boundaries.description: The separate trust zone containing the CDN and its bucket.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.

assumptions.assumption: The web server is reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it the public site and says readers hit the web server over HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The web server presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a public site and a web server serving readers.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN bucket contains publicly available content.
assumptions.basis: The source says readers fetch the published images, stylesheets, and downloads from the CDN.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN is controlled by a different party from the hosted web server and database.
assumptions.basis: The CDN is described as a separate content delivery service and its bucket is distinct from the hosted network.
